newsitem.title: UKRAINE: 1ST UKRAINE BEET TEST HAS 10.3 PCT SUGAR CONTENT.
newsitem.headline: 1ST UKRAINE BEET TEST HAS 10.3 PCT SUGAR CONTENT.

text.p: The first Ukrainian sugar beet test for 1997 showed an average sugar content of 10.3 percent, down from last year's 11.6 percent, the Agriculture Ministry said on Thursday.
The ministry gave the following data for first test, carried out on August 6, compared with the same date last year -
The government last month revised down its forecast for the 1997 sugar beet crop to 27 million tonnes from 30-31 million tonnes. Last year's crop was 24 million tonnes.
Ukraine, a major exporter of refined white sugar to Russia, had previously forecast refined sugar output of 3.26 million tonnes this year, flat on 1996 levels.
The ministry could not say when the next text would be carried out.
